newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Q1 earnings leave BUX virtually steady.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Q1 earnings leave BUX virtually steady.

text.p: Rising profits in the first quarter of the year, reported by heavy-weight Hungarian shares on Thursday, left the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) almost unchanged, traders said.
"I did not see that the results affected the bourse as a whole very much," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities.
According to preliminary figures, the BUX index finished at 5,881.55 points, up by 0.16 percent or 9.16 points.
Traders said the first quarter earnings figures did not surprise the market, and expectations of good corporate results had already been built in the prices.
The corporate results did not move the market as a whole, but helped individual shares as meat processor Pick, OTP Bank and retailer Fotex rise slightly, traders said.
Pick rose 215 forints, to close at 11,615. OTP firmed 35 forint to 4,250, while Fotex rose three forints to 134.

However, most prices moved little, and the BUX index could have been slightly negative but for some deals at the end of the session in oil and gas company MOL shares, which pushed their price up by some 40 forints, traders said.

The overall long-term outlook of BSE remained positive and good corporate results, coupled with a recovery in economic activity, were likely to increase the appetite of foreign investors for Hungarian shares, traders and an analyst said.
"We are still very optimistic with the market," said London-based HSBC analyst Nigel Rendell. "As far as the foreign investors are concerned, they are looking for the opprtunity to buy in Hungary."
The Hungarian stock market was likely to remain one of the favourites of investors looking at the region, but after recent price rises, a downward correction may come in Budapest, traders said.
"I would say there will be a decline (in prices)," said Berecz. "Good corporate results has already come out, and there will be a period without news."
He added that the investors still waited for the results of MOL, the largest capitalised stock on the BSE.
Domestic investors, who finished on Wednesday a subscription of four percent of the shares in MOL, are likely to por their shares on the BSE in the near future, traders said.
